title: The ex-Secret Service agent who flipped a hacker is now raising a second $250M cybersecurity fund
slides: Can one ex-agent turning hackers stop the next breach?
He spent years in the Secret Service hunting cybercriminals
Now he's raising a second $250M fund to back them
Founders pitching him face a harder test than most VCs
Ask: is your security product something a hacker would fear?
thread_text:
1. The ex-agent test

A former Secret Service cybercrime hunter is now raising $250M to back the hackers he used to chase. He evaluates founders harder than most VCs — here’s why.

2. Secret Service years

He spent years in the Secret Service tracking down cybercriminals. That experience gives him a playbook most investors don’t have: thinking like the attacker.

3. Second $250M fund

This is his second $250M fund. He’s not just writing checks — he’s building a portfolio of security startups that can outsmart the threats he once investigated.

4. Founders face harder test

Pitching him is tougher than most VCs. He probes for real-world resilience, not just hype. If your product wouldn’t scare a hacker, he’s not interested.

5. Ask yourself

Is your security product something a hacker would fear? If you can’t answer that, rethink your pitch. Test it against a real threat model this week.
